question: Gastric irritation is least with following NSA1D: (PGI June 2008)
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Acetaminophen" -> "minimal COX inhibition in stomach" -> "least gastric irritation" -> 95%
analysis: The question asks which NSAID causes the least gastric irritation. NSAIDs typically cause gastric irritation due to their inhibition of cyclooxygenase (COX) enzymes, which are involved in the production of protective gastric prostaglandins. Acetaminophen (paracetamol) is not a traditional NSAID as it has minimal anti-inflammatory properties and does not significantly inhibit COX enzymes in the stomach, leading to minimal gastric irritation. Diclofenac, ibuprofen, and naproxen are all traditional NSAIDs that inhibit COX enzymes to varying degrees, with naproxen generally associated with more gastric irritation due to its stronger COX inhibition. Therefore, acetaminophen is the least likely to cause gastric irritation among the options provided.
